Hello,
The main options are pretty simple:

• Blumat Classic: best for indoor houseplants and simple vacation watering. It pulls water from a nearby container and has no adjustment screw.
• Tropf-Blumat kits: best when you want a more complete automatic watering setup for multiple pots, planters, or small garden areas. A moisture-sensing ceramic carrot controls the flow, and tubing carries water to the plants from a raised reservoir or a pressure-reduced source.
• Starter gravity kits: the easiest way to begin with Tropf-Blumat. They use a raised reservoir and do not need electricity.
• Kits with a reservoir included: same idea, but easier because the water source is already part of the kit.
• Backyard or larger kits: better if you want to water more plants or outdoor areas and expand later.

If you want the simplest place to begin, the Blumat 5-Pack Starter Kit is a strong first pick for a few plants, and the Blumat 6 Sensor Drip Irrigation Kit is a good step up if you want the reservoir included.

Hello,
It uses a moisture-sensing ceramic carrot to control water flow. As the soil dries, the carrot opens and lets water move through the tubing. As the soil gets moist again, it restricts the flow.

For your first setup with this kit, use a raised reservoir, then:

Set the reservoir at least 3 feet above ground level.
Install the carrot in the growing medium with firm soil contact, ideally halfway between the pot center and wall, and no deeper than about 6 inches.
Connect the 8 mm supply tubing to the carrot, then connect the outlet to your watering points.
Keep the tubing fully seated and avoid sharp kinks.
Place the watering points around the root zone so the container gets even moisture.
Test the setup and make only small adjustments after the growing medium has had time to respond.
For a first run, this is the easiest and safest way to learn it. Happy to point you to it whenever you're ready.
